title.zh: “莱昂·布莱克躲在诉讼后面”：亿万富翁因爱泼斯坦调查中的传票而起诉国会，引发愤怒——直播

summary.en: Republican oversight chair James Comer stated he will discuss next steps with the committee, as a Democrat called for holding the billionaire in contempt for defying two subpoenas. Leon Black, a financier, has sued the oversight committee, alleging the subpoenas were improper, and has denied wrongdoing. The...
summary.zh: 共和党监督委员会主席詹姆斯·科默表示，他将与委员会讨论下一步措施，同时一名民主党人呼吁因亿万富翁无视两份传票而将其藐视法庭。亿万富翁金融家莱昂·布莱克否认有不当行为，并已起诉监督委员会，声称传票不当。该调查正在审查联邦政府数十年来未能支持杰弗里·爱泼斯坦的幸存者。

body.en: Vice president holds first press briefing since Karoline Leavitt’s departure and rebuffs Iran’s claims of deadly US strikes while defending Pete Hegseth Sign up for US Breaking News emails Republican oversight chair James Comer has also weighed in on Leon Black not sitting for a deposition about his ties to Jeffrey Epstein. The billionaire financier, who has denied wrongdoing, filed suit against the oversight committee Thursday alleging the subpoenas were improper. “It’s a shame Leon Black is hiding behind litigation rather than provide answers to the American people. Our investigation is examining how the federal government for decades failed survivors of Jeffery Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell’s crimes and how Mr. Epstein sought to curry favor with influential individuals to avoid scrutiny,” Comer said in a statement. “Mr. Black’s testimony is crucial to our investigation as he was one of Mr. Epstein’s fee paying clients and has several nondisclosure agreements.” Continue reading...
body.zh: 共和党监督主席詹姆斯·科默表示，他将就下一步行动向委员会发表讲话，因为民主党呼吁以藐视法庭罪判处亿万富翁藐视两份传票。共和党监督主席詹姆斯·科默还对莱昂·布莱克不就他与杰弗里·爱泼斯坦的关系出庭作证一事发表了意见。这位否认有不当行为的亿万富翁金融家周四对监督委员会提起诉讼，指控传票不当。 “莱昂·布莱克躲在诉讼背后，而不是向美国人民提供答案，这是一种耻辱。我们的调查正在调查几十年来联邦政府如何辜负杰弗里·爱泼斯坦和吉斯兰·麦克斯韦尔罪行的幸存者，以及爱泼斯坦先生如何寻求巴结有影响力的个人以避免审查，”科默在一份声明中说。 “布莱克先生的证词对我们的调查至关重要，因为他是爱泼斯坦先生的付费客户之一，并且签订了几项保密协议。”继续阅读...

reflection.en: In the face of serious allegations and a government investigation, financier Leon Black has resorted to legal challenges rather than providing answers. This situation raises questions about accountability and transparency, especially when the investigation concerns the welfare of survivors. The prophet Micah reminds us that true righteousness involves not...
reflection.zh: 面对严重的指控和政府的调查，金融家莱昂·布莱克选择通过法律挑战来规避，而不是提供答案。这种情况引发了关于问责制和透明度的问题，尤其当调查涉及幸存者的福祉时。先知弥迦提醒我们，真正的公义不仅在于不行恶，更在于积极追求公义和显出怜悯。

verse.textEn: What does Yahweh require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.
verse.textZh: 雅伟向你所要的是什么呢？只要你行公义，好怜悯，存谦卑的心，与你的神同行。

title.en: Hillary Clinton leads tributes to Gloria Steinem: ‘Her activism was rooted in optimism’
title.zh: 希拉里·克林顿等悼念格洛丽亚·斯泰纳姆：“她的行动主义植根于乐观主义”

summary.en: Former US Secretary of State Hillary Clinton, alongside Nancy Pelosi, Jill Biden, and Roxane Gay, led tributes to the groundbreaking feminist campaigner Gloria Steinem, who passed away at 92 in her New York City home. Clinton described Steinem as 'one of the architects of the entire structure of women’s equality,'...
summary.zh: 前美国国务卿希拉里·克林顿与南希·佩洛西、吉尔·拜登和罗克珊·盖伊等人一起，悼念了92岁在家中去世的开创性女权主义活动家格洛丽亚·斯泰纳姆。克林顿称斯泰纳姆为“塑造女性平等地位的建筑师之一”，并强调了她的乐观主义和为促进女性权利所做的毕生努力。

body.en: Ex-secretary of state joins Nancy Pelosi, Jill Biden, Roxane Gay and others in heralding groundbreaking feminist Gloria Steinem, groundbreaking feminist campaigner, dies aged 92 ‘We badly need to raise our boys more like our girls’: Gloria Steinem – a life in quotes Leading figures from politics, entertainment and wider society led glowing tributes to Gloria Steinem on Thursday, with Hillary Clinton hailing the American feminist icon who died at 92 at home in New York City as “one of the architects of the entire structure of women’s equality”. Clinton, a former US secretary of state, presidential candidate and first lady, was among the first to jump in with praise early on Thursday when she appeared on the CBS Mornings TV show to share her respect and gratitude for Steinem. Continue reading...
body.zh: 前国务卿与南希·佩洛西、吉尔·拜登、罗克珊·盖伊等人一起悼念开创性的女权主义者格洛丽亚·斯泰纳姆，享年 92 岁92 岁的她在纽约市的家中被称为“整个妇女平等结构的建筑师之一”。美国前国务卿、总统候选人和第一夫人克林顿在周四早些时候出现在哥伦比亚广播公司早间电视节目中，表达了她对斯泰纳姆的尊重和感激之情，她是最先表达赞扬的人之一。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Gloria Steinem dedicated her life to championing women's rights, a cause that often requires speaking for those whose voices have been silenced. Her activism, rooted in optimism, reminds us of the power of persistent advocacy. As Proverbs 31:8-9 urges, 'Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for all their rights.' Steinem embodied this call,...
reflection.zh: 格洛丽亚·斯泰纳姆一生致力于倡导女性权利，这项事业常常需要为那些被剥夺话语权的人发声。她的行动主义植根于乐观主义，提醒我们坚持倡导的力量。正如《箴言》31:8-9所敦促的：“本应开口为那些不能开口的辩护，为所有孤苦无凭的人伸张正义。”斯泰纳姆践行了这一呼召，致力于为所有女性争取平等和尊严。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Feminist activist and journalist Gloria Steinem dies, aged 92
title.zh: 女权活动家和记者格洛丽亚·斯泰纳姆去世，享年92岁

summary.en: Gloria Steinem, a prominent feminist activist and journalist who became a leader of the women's liberation movement in the US, has died at the age of 92. Her foundation announced she passed away peacefully at her New York City home, surrounded by loved ones. Steinem co-founded the Women's Action Alliance and Ms....
summary.zh: 美国女权运动的领袖之一、著名的女权活动家和记者格洛丽亚·斯泰纳姆（Gloria Steinem）去世，享年92岁。她的基金会宣布，她在纽约市的家中安详离世，身边有许多爱她的人。斯泰纳姆女士是妇女行动联盟和《Ms.》杂志的联合创始人，五十多年来一直倡导妇女权利和相关议题。

body.en:
Gloria Steinem, who became a leader of the women's liberation movement in the US, has died aged 92.

In a post on Instagram, her foundation said she "passed away peacefully" at her home in New York City on Wednesday, "surrounded by many who loved her".

Steinem, who was a writer and magazine editor, co-founded the Women's Action Alliance - a group dedicated to fighting sexism - more than 50 years ago.

She started her career as a journalist in New York and went on to co-found Ms. magazine, one of the first publications to focus on women's issues other than housekeeping and beauty.

During the 1970s, Steinem was a vocal campaigner for women's reproductive rights, among other causes.

She herself obtained an illegal abortion in London when she was 22 years old, and years later celebrated the US Supreme Court's 1973 ruling in the case of Roe v Wade, which granted women the constitutional right to abortion. Nearly half a century later she witnessed the reversal of this decision.

She also spoke out in favour of the legalisation of same-sex marriage, as well as equal rights and pay for women, and protested against the death penalty and female genital mutilation.

Born on 25 March 1934 in Toledo, Ohio, she had a difficult childhood and did not go to school full-time until she was 12 years old.

After university in the late 1950s, she went to India on a research scholarship and spent two years in a variety of roles, including helping village women organise non-violent protests against government policies, which sparked her interest in grassroots activism.

She then moved to New York City in the early 1960s to start her career as a freelance writer. Her big break came through an exposé of Playboy Bunny working conditions.

Eventually she became a columnist for New York Magazine, before founding Ms. magazine in 1972.

For years, Steinem famously eschewed marriage, but she went on to tie the knot in 2000 to David Bale, a South African-born entrepreneur-environmentalist and father of actor Christian Bale. He died three years later from brain lymphoma.

When questioned over why she changed her position on marriage, she replied: "I didn't change. Marriage changed."

In 2013, then-President Barack Obama awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the highest civilian honour in the US.

"Gloria's greatest gift was her ability to listen to others, to make others feel seen and heard. Her words, actions and example gave people permission to be their truest selves. Gloria lived true to her independent spirit, always with curiosity and a great sense of humour."

Her foundation said she lived her last years being in community and writing - welcoming guests into her home for "Talking Circles" - a tradition that will continue.

Her commitment to her home becoming a...
body.zh: 美国妇女解放运动领导人格洛丽亚·斯泰纳姆 (Gloria Steinem) 去世，享年 92 岁。 她的基金会在 Instagram 上发帖称，她周三在纽约市的家中“平静地去世”，“周围有许多爱她的人”。 斯坦纳姆是一名作家和杂志编辑，50 多年前与他人共同创立了妇女行动联盟，这是一个致力于对抗性别歧视的组织。 她在纽约以记者身份开始了自己的职业生涯，后来与人共同创办了《女士》杂志，这是最早关注家务和美容以外的女性问题的出版物之一。 20 世纪 70 年代，斯泰纳姆是女性生殖权利等事业的积极倡导者。 她自己22岁时在伦敦非法堕胎，多年后庆祝美国最高法院1973年对罗伊诉韦德案的裁决，该裁决赋予妇女宪法规定的堕胎权。近半个世纪后，她目睹了这一决定的逆转。 她还公开支持同性婚姻合法化以及妇女平等权利和薪酬，并抗议死刑和女性生殖器切割。 她于 1934 年 3 月 25 日出生于俄亥俄州托莱多，童年时期很艰难，直到 12 岁才开始全日制学校。 20世纪50年代末大学毕业后，她获得研究奖学金前往印度，并在两年内担任过各种职务，包括帮助乡村妇女组织反对政府政策的非暴力抗议活动，这激发了她对草根激进主义的兴趣。 20 世纪 60 年代初，她搬到纽约，开始了自由作家的职业生涯。她的重大突破来自于揭露《花花公子兔子》的工作条件。 最终，她成为《纽约杂志》的专栏作家，并于 1972 年创办《女士》杂志。 她以回避婚姻而闻名，并于 2000 年与南非出生的企业家兼环保主义者、演员克里斯蒂安·贝尔的父亲大卫·贝尔 (David Bale) 喜结良缘。三年后，他死于脑淋巴瘤。 2013年，时任总统巴拉克·奥巴马授予她美国公民最高荣誉——总统自由勋章。 “格洛丽亚最伟大的天赋是她倾听他人的能力，让别人感到被看到和听到。她的言语、行动和榜样让人们成为最真实的自己。格洛丽亚忠于她的独立精神，总是充满好奇心和幽默感。” 她的基金会表示，她的最后几年生活在社区和写作中——欢迎客人来到她家参加“谈话圈”——这一传统将继续下去。 她致力于让自己的家成为社会正义运动的中心，以及即将出版的《意外的生活》一书，是“格洛丽亚送给世界的众多礼物之一……

reflection.en: Gloria Steinem dedicated her life to amplifying the voices of women and challenging systemic sexism. Her work, including co-founding Ms. magazine, ensured that women's issues were brought to the forefront of public discourse. As we remember her, we are reminded of the enduring call to speak for the voiceless and advocate for justice.
reflection.zh: 格洛丽亚·斯泰纳姆将一生奉献给放大女性的声音，并挑战系统性的性别歧视。她的工作，包括与人合创《Ms.》杂志，确保了女性议题被推到公共讨论的前沿。当我们缅怀她时，我们被提醒要永远为无声者发声，倡导公正。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Far-right Israeli minister outlines plan for removal of all Palestinians from Gaza
title.zh: 以色列极右翼部长概述了将所有巴勒斯坦人迁出加沙的计划

summary.en: Israel's far-right national security minister has outlined a plan for the illegal forced expulsion of all Palestinians from the Gaza Strip, aiming to remove 250,000 in the first year and the rest of the 2 million population over six years.
summary.zh: 以色列极右翼国家安全部长概述了一项非法强制驱逐加沙地带所有巴勒斯坦人的计划，目标是在第一年内迁移25万人，并在六年内迁移其余约200万人口。

body.en: Itamar Ben-Gvir claims proposal for illegal forced displacement of 2 million people is ‘realistic’ and ‘concrete’ Israel’s far-right national security minister has set out a plan for the illegal forced expulsion of all Palestinians from the Gaza Strip, with the intention of sending them abroad. Speaking in the run-up to close-fought Israeli elections, Itamar Ben-Gvir said the plan aimed to remove 250,000 Palestinians from Gaza in the first year, followed by the rest of its population of roughly 2 million over the next six years. Continue reading...
body.zh: 伊塔马尔·本-格维尔声称，非法强迫200万人流离失所的提议是“现实的”和“具体的”。以色列极右翼国家安全部长已经制定了一项计划，将所有巴勒斯坦人非法强制驱逐出加沙地带，目的是将他们送往国外。伊塔马尔·本-格维尔在势均力敌的以色列选举前夕发表讲话时表示，该计划的目标是在第一年将 25 万巴勒斯坦人从加沙地带撤离，然后在未来六年内将约 200 万剩余的巴勒斯坦人撤离加沙。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The proposal by Itamar Ben-Gvir to forcibly displace 2 million Palestinians from Gaza represents a profound disregard for human dignity and rights. Such plans, driven by a desire for ethnic cleansing, echo the actions of tyrants throughout history who have abused power to oppress and displace entire populations. The Bible warns against such wickedness,...
reflection.zh: 伊塔马尔·本-格维尔提出的强制驱逐加沙200万巴勒斯坦人的计划，是对人类尊严和权利的严重漠视。这种出于种族清洗的意图的计划，呼应了历史上那些滥用权力压迫和流离失所整个人口的暴君的行为。圣经警告要警惕这种邪恶，提醒我们统治者要为自己的行为负责。

verse.textEn: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.
verse.textZh: 暴虐的君王辖制贫民，好像吼叫的狮子、觅食的熊。

title.en: Hundreds gather to urge Scottish government to pause datacentre boom
title.zh: 数百人聚集敦促苏格兰政府暂停数据中心热潮

summary.en: Hundreds of people gathered in Edinburgh to call for an immediate moratorium on Scotland's datacentre boom, with at least 20 projects proposed. One project in Auchtertool, Fife, is reportedly the second largest in the world. Activists, like Kat Jones, are leading the opposition.
summary.zh: 数百人在爱丁堡集会，呼吁立即暂停苏格兰的数据中心热潮，目前已有至少20个项目被提议。位于法夫郡奥克特图尔的一个项目据称是世界第二大。活动人士，如凯特·琼斯，正在领导反对活动。

body.en: Opposition mounts as at least 20 projects proposed, including one in Fife billed as second largest in world Kat Jones may be the closest thing Scotland has to Erin Brockovich in 2026. Standing in the shadow of Arthur’s Seat outside Holyrood, the 52-year-old is revving up the crowd of protesters around her. “Who is here from Lammermuir? Ayrshire? What about Aberdeen?” she calls to the crowd. On Thursday, hundreds travelled to Edinburgh to call for an immediate moratorium on Scotland’s datacentre boom, which includes one project in Auchtertool, Fife, that has been billed as the second largest in the world. Continue reading...
body.zh: 至少有 20 个拟议项目遭到反对，其中包括号称世界第二大的法夫郡的一个项目。凯特·琼斯 (Kat Jones) 可能是 2026 年苏格兰最接近艾琳·布罗科维奇 (Erin Brockovich) 的项目。这位 52 岁的女士站在荷里路德外亚瑟王宝座的阴影下，让周围的抗议者兴奋不已。 “谁来自拉默缪尔？艾尔郡？阿伯丁呢？”她向人群喊道。周四，数百人前往爱丁堡，呼吁立即暂停苏格兰数据中心的繁荣，其中包括位于法夫郡奥赫特图尔​​的一个项目，该项目被誉为世界第二大数据中心。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The gathering in Edinburgh highlights a community's deep concern over the rapid expansion of datacentres and its potential impact. Their collective voice rises, echoing the ancient call for justice to flow like a river, a powerful current that shapes the land and sustains life. May their advocacy bring about thoughtful consideration and equitable solutions...
reflection.zh: 在爱丁堡的集会凸显了社区对数据中心快速扩张及其潜在影响的深切担忧。他们的集体声音响起，呼应了古老的呼吁，愿公义如江河滚滚，成为塑造大地、滋养生命的强大力量。愿他们的倡导为苏格兰的未来带来深思熟虑的考量和公平的解决方案。

verse.textEn: Let justice roll on like a river, righteousness like a never-failing stream!
verse.textZh: 惟愿公平如大水滚滚，使公义如江河滔滔。

title.en: Serbians targeted with spyware in country’s ‘largest documented wave of surveillance’
title.zh: 塞尔维亚人成为该国“迄今为止记录在案的最大规模监控”的间谍软件目标

summary.en: Digital rights group Share Foundation reports that at least 14 individuals from Serbian civil society, including student protesters, were targeted with advanced spyware earlier this year. This marks the largest documented wave of such infections in Serbia. The discovery followed Apple's notification to users in 110...
summary.zh: 数字权利组织Share Foundation报告称，今年早些时候，包括学生抗议者在内的至少14名塞尔维亚公民社会成员成为高级间谍软件的目标。这标志着塞尔维亚此类感染的记录在案的最大规模浪潮。此前，苹果公司已通知110个国家的数百万用户可能遭受了雇佣间谍软件的攻击。塞尔维亚政府否认了间谍活动。

body.en: Student protesters among those hacked, says digital rights group, though Aleksandar Vučić’s government denies spying At least 14 people from across Serbian civil society were targeted with advanced spyware earlier this year in what the digital rights group Share Foundation said was the largest documented ​wave of such infection in Serbia to date. The wave of spyware infections was discovered in August after Apple notified people in 110 ⁠countries that they had probably been victims ⁠of mercenary spyware. Continue reading...
body.zh: 数字权利组织表示，遭到黑客攻击的人中包括学生抗议者，但亚历山大·武契奇政府否认从事间谍活动。今年早些时候，来自塞尔维亚民间社会的至少 14 人成为先进间谍软件的目标，数字权利组织共享基金会称，这是塞尔维亚迄今为止记录在案的最大规模此类感染浪潮。 8 月份，苹果公司通知 110 个国家/地区的人们，他们可能是雇佣间谍软件的受害者，之后发现了间谍软件感染浪潮。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The discovery of advanced spyware targeting at least 14 individuals in Serbia, including student protesters, raises grave concerns about state surveillance and the erosion of civil liberties. Such actions, when wielded by those in power, can silence dissent and create an atmosphere of fear, mirroring the oppressive nature of tyranny. The pursuit of truth...
reflection.zh: 在塞尔维亚，包括学生抗议者在内的至少14人成为高级间谍软件的目标，这一发现引发了对国家监控和公民自由被侵蚀的严重担忧。当权力掌握在当权者手中时，此类行为会压制异议，制造恐惧气氛，与暴政的压迫性本质相呼应。追求真理和正义需要警惕此类滥用行为。

verse.textEn: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.

title.en: Trump's Iran strategy: Could this become a forever war?
title.zh: 特朗普的伊朗战略：这会变成一场永恒的战争吗？

summary.en: The US has launched fresh attacks on military targets in Iran, aiming to prevent Tehran from rebuilding its destroyed capabilities. However, this risks triggering a sustained downward spiral of reconstruction followed by new attacks.
summary.zh: 美国对伊朗的军事目标发动了新的袭击，旨在阻止德黑兰重建其被摧毁的能力。然而，这可能会引发一个持续的恶性循环：重建、然后是新的袭击。

body.en:
The US has launched fresh attacks on military targets in Iran. It wants to prevent Tehran rebuilding its destroyed capabilities, but risks triggering a sustained downward spiral of reconstruction followed by new attacks.

US president Donald Trump has given a fairly clear description of what the next phase of the Iran war could look like. The Iranians had tried to rebuild their radar equipment, Trump stated after the most recent wave of US strikes . "We waited until it was almost built, and then we hit it," he said.

On Tuesday, American forces once again attacked several targets in Iran . According to US Central Command (CENTCOM), the targets destroyed included "air defense sites, radar systems, maritime assets and facilities, mine laying capabilities, and communications sites."

Iran responded by firing rockets and drones at US facilities in the region. With this, the war moved on to what CENTCOM had indicated just a few days earlier could be the strategy for the next phase.

According to the news portal Axios, it was considering limited strikes, at regular intervals if necessary, to prevent Iran from reconstituting its military capabilities in the Strait of Hormuz . An American government representative used a concept from Israeli security policy to describe this idea: He called it "mowing the grass."

The metaphor refers to a strategy that doesn't even attempt to promise that an opponent will be defeated once and for all. It is enough to regularly reduce the enemy's military capabilities to the point where the threat remains manageable. When the grass grows back, you "mow" it again.

Applied to the situation in Iran, this would mean the US keeping an eye on which military capabilities the enemy is reconstituting, and attacking once it crosses a certain threshold.

In the past few months, the US has scored some military successes. US forces have significantly reduced Iran's military capabilities in the Strait of Hormuz, and have begun clearing Iranian sea mines.

However, these successes will not last. Tehran is repairing or procuring new radar installations, anti-aircraft positions, and anti-ship missiles. US bombs could certainly destroy important Iranian positions with targeted strikes. But the knowledge and the industrial basis of Iranian military technology would remain.

Reconstruction can therefore be delayed, but not prevented. The US will repeatedly be confronted with the same choice: whether to accept that Tehran is regaining its capabilities, or to attack again and destroy them.

Mona Yacoubian, director of the Middle East program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) in Washington, warned as early as April that this development could lead to an "enduring low-intensity conflict punctuated by more intensive...
body.zh: 美国对伊朗的军事目标发动了新的袭击。它希望阻止德黑兰重建其被摧毁的能力，但有可能引发重建工作持续螺旋式下降，进而引发新的袭击。 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普对伊朗战争的下一阶段可能会是什么样子给出了相当明确的描述。特朗普在美国最近一波袭击后表示，伊朗人曾试图重建他们的雷达设备。 “我们一直等到它快建成了，然后我们就开始了，”他说。 周二，美军再次袭击了伊朗的多个目标。据美国中央司令部（CENTCOM）称，被摧毁的目标包括“防空站点、雷达系统、海上资产和设施、布雷能力和通信站点”。 伊朗向美国在该地区的设施发射火箭和无人机作为回应。至此，战争转向了中央司令部几天前表示的下一阶段的战略。 据新闻门户网站 Axios 报道，伊朗正在考虑进行有限的打击，并在必要时定期进行打击，以阻止伊朗在霍尔木兹海峡重建其军事能力。一位美国政府代表用以色列安全政策中的一个概念来描述这个想法：他称之为“割草”。 这个比喻指的是一种甚至不试图承诺彻底击败对手的策略。定期将敌人的军事能力降低到威胁可控的程度就足够了。当草重新长出来时，你再次“修剪”它。 应用于伊朗局势，这意味着美国密切关注敌人正在重组哪些军事能力，一旦超过一定阈值就发动攻击。 过去几个月，美国取得了一些军事胜利。美军大幅削弱了伊朗在霍尔木兹海峡的军事能力，并开始清除伊朗的海雷。 然而，这些成功不会持续下去。德黑兰正在修复或采购新的雷达装置、防空阵地和反舰导弹。美国的炸弹肯定可以通过有针对性的打击摧毁伊朗的重要阵地。但伊朗军事技术的知识和工业基础将保留。 因此，重建可以被推迟，但不能被阻止。美国将反复面临同样的选择：是接受德黑兰正在恢复其能力，还是再次攻击并摧毁它们。 华盛顿战略与国际研究中心 (CSIS) 中东项目主任莫娜·雅库比安 (Mona Yacoubian) 早在 4 月份就警告称，这一事态发展可能会导致“持久的低强度冲突，其间夹杂着更激烈的……

reflection.en: The news describes a cycle of destruction and rebuilding, where each strike is met with efforts to restore capabilities, only to be targeted again. This pattern of action and reaction risks a perpetual conflict. The ancient wisdom calls us to break this cycle, not by mirroring the aggression, but by choosing a different path, seeking to overcome destructive...
reflection.zh: 新闻描述了一个破坏与重建的循环，每一次打击都伴随着恢复能力的努力，却又招致新的打击。这种反复的行动和反应模式，有陷入永久冲突的风险。古老的智慧呼唤我们打破这个循环，不是通过模仿侵略，而是选择一条不同的道路，努力用建设性的、生命肯定的行动来克服破坏性的模式。

verse.textEn: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
verse.textZh: 你不可为恶所胜，反要以善胜恶。

title.en: Trump $1 coin makes him first living president on US currency in a century
title.zh: 特朗普一美元硬币使其成为一个世纪以来首位出现在美国货币上的在世总统

summary.en: The US Mint has released a special edition $1 coin featuring a portrait of Donald Trump, marking the first time a living president has appeared on US currency in a century. This was made possible by a legislative clause for the nation's 250th anniversary, bypassing a law that typically prohibits living presidents from...
summary.zh: 美国铸币局推出了一款特别版一美元硬币，上面印有唐纳德·特朗普的肖像，这是近一个世纪以来首位在世总统出现在美国货币上。这一举措得益于一项为纪念美国250周年而设的立法条款，绕过了通常禁止在世总统出现在硬币上的法律。这些硬币是作为收藏品发行的，并非用于日常流通。

body.en:
Donald Trump's portrait has made its way on to a US coin - the latest move by the president to put his personal stamp on American institutions.

On Wednesday, the US Mint launched the $1 (£0.74) coin with a portrait of Trump alongside the words "Liberty" and "In God We Trust", to celebrate America's 250th anniversary.

The Mint said the coins, which are being marketed as a collectable, were not being put into circulation for daily use.

The law bans living presidents from appearing on US currency, but a design clause in legislation for the anniversary was used to overcome this.

The coins - priced at $61 for a roll of 25 and $154.50 for a bag of 100 - were "not currently in stock" on the mint's website within hours of going on sale but it said more are being made.

The coins were also being sold in vending machines at the US Mint store in Washington DC.

The BBC has contacted the US Mint, the Treasury and the White House for further details.

The coin has been "created to celebrate this historic national milestone" with a "once-in-a-generation anniversary design destined to become a standout addition to modern collections", the US Mint said.

The coins have a golden colour but do not contain any actual gold. According to the US Mint, they are 88.5% copper with the balance being made up of zinc, nickel and a manganese brass outer layer.

While they are not in circulation, they can be used as legal tender to pay off debt and taxes, although federal law states that businesses can decide whether or not to accept them.

In May, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said his department was planning to issue a new $250 bill bearing a portrait of President Trump .

At the time, Bessent highlighted that another living US president has previously appeared on the country's currency.

A half-dollar that was issued to commemorate America's 150th anniversary in 1926 featured then-President Calvin Coolidge.

The Trump administration has also cited the Circulating Collectible Coin Redesign Act of 2020, from Trump's first term.

While this statute prohibits portraits of living people on the reverse (tails side) of coins, it does not explicitly cover the obverse (heads side), where Trump's likeness appears on the new $1 coins.

In March, the Treasury announced that US paper money would soon bear Trump's signature - another first for a sitting US president.
body.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普的肖像被印在美国硬币上——这是总统在美国机构上打上个人印记的最新举措。 周三，美国造币厂推出了 1 美元（0.74 英镑）硬币，上面印有特朗普的肖像，旁边写着“自由”和“我们信仰上帝”字样，以庆祝美国成立 250 周年。 造币厂表示，这些硬币作为收藏品销售，并未投入日常使用流通。 该法律禁止在世总统出现在美元上，但周年纪念立法中的设计条款被用来克服这一问题。 这些硬币每卷 25 枚售价为 61 美元，每袋 100 枚售价为 154.50 美元，在发售后数小时内，造币厂网站上“目前没有库存”，但该公司表示正在制作更多硬币。 这些硬币还在华盛顿特区的美国造币厂商店的自动售货机中出售。 BBC 已联系美国造币厂、财政部和白宫了解更多细节。 美国造币厂表示，这枚硬币的设计是为了“庆祝这一历史性的国家里程碑”，其“一代周年纪念设计注定会成为现代收藏的杰出补充”。 这些硬币呈金色，但不含任何实际黄金。据美国造币厂称，它们的成分为 88.5% 铜，其余部分由锌、镍和锰黄铜外层组成。 虽然它们不流通，但可以用作偿还债务和税收的法定货币，尽管联邦法律规定企业可以决定是否接受它们。 5 月，财政部长斯科特·贝森特表示，他的部门计划发行印有特朗普总统肖像的新版 250 美元钞票。 当时，贝森特强调，另一位在世的美国总统此前曾出现在该国的货币上。 1926 年为纪念美国成立 150 周年而发行的半美元硬币上刻有时任总统卡尔文·柯立芝的头像。 特朗普政府还引用了特朗普第一任期内的《2020 年流通收藏币重新设计法案》。 虽然该法规禁止在硬币的反面（反面）上绘制活人肖像，但它并没有明确涵盖正面（正面），特朗普的肖像出现在新的 1 美元硬币上。 今年三月，财政部宣布美国纸币很快将有特朗普的签名——这对在任美国总统来说又是第一次。

reflection.en: The appearance of a living president's portrait on US currency, even as a collectible, raises questions about national identity and the values we choose to memorialize. Proverbs 14:34 reminds us that national character is deeply intertwined with righteousness, suggesting that true national strength and honor are found in ethical governance and justice, not...
reflection.zh: 在美元硬币上印在世总统的肖像，即使是作为收藏品，也引发了关于国家身份和我们选择纪念的价值观的问题。《箴言》14章34节提醒我们，国家的品格与公义息息相关，这表明真正的国家力量和荣耀在于道德治理和公正，而不仅仅是象征性的表现。

verse.textEn: Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin condemns any people.
verse.textZh: 公义使邦国高举；罪恶是人民的羞辱。

title.en: Norway seizes Russian ship in Svalbard to compensate Ukraine
title.zh: 挪威扣押俄罗斯船只以赔偿乌克兰

summary.en: Norway has seized a Russian ship, the Professor Molchanov, under a court order obtained by Ukraine's Naftogaz. This action is a consequence of Russia's refusal to pay damages awarded to Naftogaz following Moscow's seizure of assets in Crimea in 2014. Russia has protested the seizure.
summary.zh: 挪威根据乌克兰Naftogaz公司获得的法院命令，扣押了一艘俄罗斯船只“莫尔恰诺夫教授”号。此举源于俄罗斯拒绝支付在2014年莫斯科吞并克里米亚后，被判给Naftogaz的赔偿金。俄罗斯已对此扣押提出抗议。

body.zh: 挪威当局根据 Naftogaz 在乌克兰寻求并获得的法院命令扣押了一艘俄罗斯船只“Professor Molchanov”。俄罗斯对此举表示抗议，因为俄罗斯拒绝支付 Naftogaz 的损失。 挪威法院下令在北极扣押一艘俄罗斯船只，以执行乌克兰国家能源公司 Naftogaz 在莫斯科扣押其在克里米亚（俄罗斯于 2014 年非法吞并克里米亚）的资产后赢得的 42.2 亿美元（约合 36 亿欧元）赔偿索赔的一部分。 官员们宣布，周三晚间，该船已被阻止离开位于斯瓦尔巴群岛巴伦支堡的俄罗斯煤矿定居点的港口。 斯瓦尔巴群岛自 1925 年以来一直是挪威领土，但它是一个非军事区，来自包括俄罗斯在内的数十个国家的人们可以在某些条件下免签证定居。 俄罗斯驻挪威大使表示，莫斯科将通过法律途径寻求释放该船。 第一个宣布该船被扣押的团体是代表 Naftogaz 的美国律师事务所卡温顿 (Covington)，该律师事务所试图确保海牙常设仲裁法院于 2023 年给予其赔偿。 在与乌克兰持续的战争中，俄罗斯拒绝支付罚款、法律费用和利息，Naftogaz 此后开始尝试通过当地法院扣押并强制出售俄罗斯商业资产。 Naftogaz 代理首席执行官 Sergii Fedorenko 表示：“俄罗斯不能仅仅通过拒绝遵守国际仲裁裁决来逃避责任。” 卡温顿表示，几个月来，它一直在追踪这艘名为“莫尔查诺夫教授”号的船。该公司表示，其申请周一获得了北特罗姆斯和塞尼亚地区法院的批准，该法院命令斯瓦尔巴群岛州长确保该船抵达后留在码头。 斯瓦尔巴群岛总督办公室随后发表声明，确认该船已被扣押，并将被扣押在斯瓦尔巴群岛。 声明称：“州长将与 Trust Arktikugol 合作，照顾船上的船员和乘客。”Trust Arktikugol 指的是管理巴伦支堡采矿定居点的俄罗斯企业（意为“北极煤炭”）。 与此同时，挪威司法部表示，该问题与奥斯陆政府没有直接关系。 司法部表示：“俄罗斯可以要求地区法院重新评估此案。” 俄罗斯驻挪威大使尼古拉·科尔丘诺夫周四在一份声明中表示，莫斯科将通过法律渠道寻求释放该船。 他说：“我们坚持要求立即释放该船，并确保乘客和船员的安全。” 克里姆林宫还召见挪威驻莫斯科大使，提出正式...

reflection.en: The seizure of the Professor Molchanov ship illustrates a complex legal and financial dispute stemming from geopolitical conflict. It brings to the fore the struggle for justice and compensation when international relations are strained, highlighting how past actions, like the annexation of Crimea, continue to have repercussions years later.
reflection.zh: “莫尔恰诺夫教授”号船只被扣押的事件，凸显了地缘政治冲突引发的复杂法律和金融纠纷。它将人们的注意力引向了在国际关系紧张时，为寻求正义和赔偿所做的斗争，并表明了像2014年吞并克里米亚这样的过往行为，多年后仍会产生持续的影响。

verse.textEn: The law is paralyzed, and justice never prevails. The wicked hem in the righteous, so that justice is perverted.
verse.textZh: 因此律法放松，公理也不显明；恶人围困义人，所以公理显然颠倒。

title.en: Palestinian teens killed during settler attack on West Bank village, officials say
title.zh: 以色列定居者袭击西岸村庄致巴勒斯坦青少年死亡，官员称

summary.en: Al-Mughayyir's council says they were trying to stop settlers stealing sheep, but the Israeli military says they threw stones at its troops. Funerals have taken place for two Palestinian teenagers who local officials say were killed by Israeli settlers and soldiers in an attack on their village in the occupied West...
summary.zh: Al-Mughayyir村委会表示，他们试图阻止定居者偷窃羊只，但以色列军方称他们向部队投掷石块。周三，在被占领的西岸，两名巴勒斯坦青少年在一次袭击中被以色列定居者和士兵杀害，当地官员称，他们的葬礼已经举行。

body.en:
Funerals have taken place for two Palestinian teenagers who local officials say were killed by Israeli settlers and soldiers in an attack on their village in the occupied West Bank on Wednesday.

The village council in al-Mughayyir told the BBC that Omar al-Nassan, 19, and Khalil Abu Alia, 16, were killed as they tried to stop Israeli settlers stealing sheep and that confrontations broke out.

The Israeli military stated that its forces had entered the village to provide security for an Israeli civilian and police trying to retrieve livestock.

It said the forces fired on and struck what it called "key instigators" of a "violent disturbance", in which Palestinians threw stones at its troops.

The deaths come amid a recent surge in settler violence in the West Bank, with more than three attacks per day on average recorded by the UN so far this year.

WhatsApp messages in groups used by settlers have indicated that they hope to force its population to move.

At least 81 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli forces or settlers in the West Bank since the start of the year, according to the UN's figures. At least 23 of those deaths have occurred in the context of settler attacks.

Three Israelis, both security forces and civilians, have been killed by Palestinians in the West Bank over the same period, the UN says.

The Israeli military has faced mounting criticism for actively participating in settler attacks on Palestinians, standing by, or failing to prosecute those responsible.

On Thursday, Israel's police force said a 19-year-old settler had been arrested on suspicion of participating in an attack on the Palestinian village of Qusra on Saturday. It marks the first such arrest in weeks of attacks on Qusra.

Dozens of masked settlers descended on the village, surrounding a house while Palestinians were trapped inside, and throwing stones.

Israeli soldiers who were deployed to the scene reportedly detained the trapped Palestinians but not the settlers, allowing them to leave. The Israeli military said troops removed "rioters" and protected residents.

Israel has built about 160 settlements housing 700,000 Jews since it occupied the West Bank and East Jerusalem - land Palestinians want, along with Gaza, for a future state - during the 1967 Middle East war. An estimated 3.3 million Palestinians live alongside them.

In a separate development on Wednesday, Israeli forces demolished the Palestinian village of Khirbet al-Tabban, in the Masafer Yatta area.

Israeli human rights group B'Tselem said the village's 70 residents, including 28 children, were given no warning prior to the demolition and were not allowed to remove their property.

It described the demolition as the most significant in Masafer Yatta since May 2025.

body.zh: 两名巴勒斯坦青少年的葬礼已经举行，当地官员称，他们在周三被以色列定居者和士兵袭击的被占领约旦河西岸村庄中丧生。 穆加耶尔村委员会告诉 BBC，19 岁的奥马尔·纳桑和 16 岁的哈利勒·阿布·阿利亚在试图阻止以色列定居者偷羊时被杀，并爆发了对抗。 以色列军方表示，其部队进入该村庄是为了为试图取回牲畜的以色列平民和警察提供安全保障。 声明称，部队向所谓的“暴力骚乱”的“主要煽动者”开火并打击，巴勒斯坦人向其部队投掷石块。 这些死亡事件发生之际，约旦河西岸定居者暴力事件最近激增，今年迄今为止，联合国记录的平均每天发生超过三起袭击事件。 定居者使用的群组中的 WhatsApp 消息表明，他们希望迫使居民迁移。 根据联合国的数据，自今年年初以来，至少有 81 名巴勒斯坦人在约旦河西岸被以色列军队或定居者杀害。其中至少 23 人死于定居者袭击。 联合国称，同一时期，三名以色列人，包括安全部队和平民，在西岸被巴勒斯坦人杀害。 以色列军方因积极参与定居者对巴勒斯坦人的袭击、袖手旁观或未能起诉责任人而面临越来越多的批评。 周四，以色列警方表示，一名 19 岁的定居者因涉嫌参与周六对巴勒斯坦村庄库斯拉的袭击而被捕。这是 Qusra 遭受袭击数周以来首次此类逮捕。 数十名蒙面定居者突然袭击村庄，包围了一座房屋，巴勒斯坦人被困在里面，并投掷石块。 据报道，部署到现场的以色列士兵拘留了被困的巴勒斯坦人，但没有拘留定居者，让他们离开。以色列军方表示，部队驱散了“骚乱者”并保护了居民。 自 1967 年中东战争期间占领约旦河西岸和东耶路撒冷以来，以色列已建造了约 160 个定居点，容纳了 70 万犹太人。巴勒斯坦人希望这片土地与加沙一起建立未来的国家。据估计，有 330 万巴勒斯坦人与他们生活在一起。 在周三的另一项进展中，以色列军队摧毁了位于 Masafer Yatta 地区的巴勒斯坦村庄 Khirbet al-Tabban。 以色列人权组织 B'Tselem 表示，该村的 70 名居民（包括 28 名儿童）在拆除之前没有收到警告，也不被允许搬走他们的财产。 据称，此次拆除是自 2025 年 5 月以来 Masafer Yatta 发生的最重大的拆除事件。 20世纪80年代，以色列...

reflection.en: The deaths of Omar al-Nassan, 19, and Khalil Abu Alia, 16, in al-Mughayyir highlight the tragic cycle of violence that plagues the region. The temptation to respond to harm with further harm is powerful, yet Scripture calls us to a higher path. May Yahweh grant wisdom and restraint to all involved, that the cycle of retaliation might be broken by acts of...
reflection.zh: 在Al-Mughayyir村，19岁的Omar al-Nassan和16岁的Khalil Abu Alia的死亡，凸显了该地区饱受困扰的悲剧性暴力循环。以暴制暴的诱惑是巨大的，但圣经呼唤我们走上一条更高的道路。愿雅伟赐予所有相关方智慧和克制，使善行能够打破报复的循环。

title.en: US sanctions halt TOEFL and GRE tests in Iran, disrupting study plans
title.zh: 美国制裁叫停伊朗托福和GRE考试，打乱留学计划

summary.en: Students in Iran are unable to take TOEFL and GRE exams due to the suspension of a US sanctions exemption. Applicants report that this decision jeopardizes their university application deadlines and imposes costly travel requirements.
summary.zh: 由于美国制裁豁免被暂停，伊朗学生无法参加托福和GRE考试。申请者表示，此举威胁到他们的大学申请截止日期，并增加了昂贵的旅行负担。

body.en:
Students in Iran can no longer take English-language proficiency exams after the suspension of a US sanctions exemption. Applicants say the move threatens university deadlines and adds costly travel obligations.

Iranian students hoping to study abroad are facing a new obstacle after TOEFL and GRE testing was suspended inside the country following changes to US sanctions regulations .

"My entire plan was built around taking this exam," a TOEFL candidate in Tehran told DW.

She said she had spent months preparing applications for a Ph.D. program, contacting professors and gathering documents despite internet disruptions and other challenges.

ETS, the US-based organization that administers both English-language proficiency exams, announced it suspended testing in Iran after the US Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) froze General License G, which had allowed certain educational services to continue in Iran .

"Following OFAC's suspension of General License G, ETS has paused administration of the TOEFL and GRE tests in Iran effective immediately," the organization said in an official notice.

ETS added that Iranian nationals can still take the exams outside Iran and that it is exploring options to restore testing.

TOEFL is a US-based English-language proficiency test accepted by universities worldwide. The GRE is a standardized test required by some graduate programs, particularly in the United States and Canada.

Since the  Iran war  began in late February, the US has increasingly expanded sanctions targeting Iranian trade and exports, contributing to broader disruptions throughout the Iranian economy .

An Iranian institution that administered TOEFL exams told DW that new registrations had stopped following the latest sanctions changes .

The institution added that the suspension could be temporary, but no date had been given for exams to resume.

That uncertainty is particularly serious for students approaching university and scholarship deadlines who have spent months preparing and paying application-related costs.

The suspension follows earlier problems with IELTS (British equivalent of TOEFL) testing in Iran. An IELTS center in Tehran  told DW that sanctions-related difficulties transferring money had become one of the main obstacles to continuing exams.

Some Iranian applicants had already been traveling to countries such as Turkey and Armenia to take IELTS. TOEFL and GRE candidates may now have to do the same.

Alireza, who is preparing to apply to a university in Italy, said the suspension of TOEFL had disrupted a backup plan he had arranged after IELTS testing became unavailable.

"European universities usually accept IELTS. But because IELTS has been suspended in Iran, after...
body.zh: 在美国制裁豁免暂停后，伊朗的学生不能再参加托福和GRE考试。申请人表示，此举威胁到大学的最后期限，并增加了昂贵的旅行义务。希望出国留学的伊朗学生在美国制裁法规变更后，托福和GRE考试在国内暂停后面临新的障碍。“我的整个计划都是围绕着参加这次考试制定的，”德黑兰的一名托福考生告诉DW。她说，尽管互联网中断和其他挑战，她还是花了几个月的时间准备博士学位课程的申请，联系教授并收集文件。管理这两项考试的美国组织ETS宣布，在美国财政部外国资产控制办公室（ OFAC ）冻结通用许可证G后，它暂停了在伊朗的考试，该许可证允许某些教育服务继续在伊朗进行。“在OFAC暂停通用许可证G之后， ETS已暂停在伊朗进行托福和GRE考试，立即生效，”该组织在一份官方通知中表示。ETS补充说，伊朗国民仍然可以在伊朗境外参加考试，并且正在探索恢复测试的选项。托福是全球各大学接受的美国英语水平考试。GRE也由同一个美国组织管理，是一些研究生课程要求的标准化考试，特别是在美国和加拿大。自2月下旬伊朗战争开始以来，美国越来越多地扩大针对伊朗贸易和出口的制裁，导致整个伊朗经济出现更广泛的混乱。一家管理托福考试的伊朗机构告诉德国之声，在最近的制裁变更后，新的注册已经停止。该机构补充说，暂停考试可能是暂时的，但没有给出恢复考试的日期。对于接近大学和奖学金截止日期的学生来说，这种不确定性尤其严重，他们花了数月时间准备文件，联系教授并支付与申请相关的费用。此前，伊朗雅思（英国相当于托福）考试出现了问题。德黑兰雅思考试中心告诉德国之声，与制裁有关的转账困难已成为继续考试的主要障碍之一。一些伊朗申请人已经前往土耳其和亚美尼亚等国家参加雅思考试。托福和GRE考生现在可能必须做同样的事情。准备申请意大利一所大学的Alireza表示，暂停托福考试打乱了他在雅思考试不可用后安排的备考计划。“欧洲大学通常接受雅思考试。但由于雅思考试已被暂停...

reflection.en: The suspension of TOEFL and GRE tests in Iran, a consequence of US sanctions, leaves many students in a difficult position, threatening their academic timelines and forcing them to incur additional expenses. These students, who have worked diligently to prepare their applications, find their voices unheard and their futures uncertain due to decisions made...
reflection.zh: 美国制裁暂停了伊朗的托福和GRE考试，这使得许多学生陷入困境，威胁到他们的学业时间表，并迫使他们承担额外费用。这些学生辛勤准备申请材料，却发现自己的声音被忽视，未来变得不确定，这一切都源于远方的决定。《箴言》31:8-9呼吁我们“为不能说话的开口，为所有孤苦者辨明是非”。这段经文提醒我们要为那些机会受到不公正限制的人们发声。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Anthony Joshua's driver attempted overtake before fatal crash, trial hears
title.zh: 安东尼·约书亚的司机在致命车祸前试图超车，审判听闻

summary.en: Adeniyi Mobolaji Kayode is charged in Nigeria with offences including causing death by dangerous driving.
summary.zh: 阿德尼伊·莫博拉吉·卡约德在尼日利亚被控包括危险驾驶致死在内的罪名。

body.en:
The driver of a car carrying Anthony Joshua was attempting to overtake another vehicle when it crashed, killing two of the boxer's friends, a court in Nigeria has heard.

Adeniyi Mobolaji Kayode, 46, faces charges including causing death by dangerous driving and driving without a valid national driver's licence. He denies the charges.

The court was told that the group - who had been travelling to visit Joshua's father in Ogun State, near Lagos in Nigeria, last December - were asleep when Kayode lost control of his Lexus SUV while he overtook a moving truck and collided with a parked lorry.

Joshua's personal trainer, Latif Ayodele, and strength coach, Sina Ghami, died in the crash.

A second defendant Abubakar Adamu, 35, the driver of the stationary lorry the car collided with, denies a charge against him of obstructing the free flow of traffic.

Inspector Christopher Ajayi Taiwo of the Ogun State Motor Traffic Division told the court that by the time he arrived at the scene, both the damaged Lexus and the stationary lorry had been removed.

But debris from the crash and soya beans scattered on the road from the lorry's load were found by officers, he added.

The only items recovered from the Lexus were a logbook, painkillers and an energy drink, which were found near the driver's side, Ajayi said.

The court heard police has yet to take a statement from Joshua following the crash.

During cross-examination, Kayode's lawyer questioned Ajayi over the lack of statement, to which he replied that "efforts are ongoing" and that he had not contacted Joshua because he "didn't have his number".

Joshua, who was born in Watford, has family roots in Sagamu - a town in Ogun state, near the crash site.

After the collision, the boxer posted a tribute to Ghami and Ayodele on social media.

"I'll just be walking with them and cracking jokes with them, not even knowing God kept me in the presence of great men.
body.zh: 尼日利亚一家法院获悉，载有安东尼·约书亚的一辆汽车的司机在试图超越另一辆车时发生车祸，导致拳击手的两名朋友死亡。 46 岁的阿德尼伊·莫博拉吉·卡约德 (Adeniyi Mobolaji Kayode) 面临危险驾驶致人死亡和无有效国家驾照驾驶等指控。他否认这些指控。 法庭获悉，去年 12 月，这群人前往尼日利亚拉各斯附近的奥贡州探望约书亚的父亲，当时他们正在睡觉，卡约德在超越一辆行驶中的卡车时失去了对他的雷克萨斯 SUV 的控制，并与一辆停放的卡车相撞。 约书亚的私人教练拉蒂夫·阿约德勒和力量教练西娜·加米在事故中丧生。 第二名被告阿布巴卡尔·阿达姆 (Abubakar Adamu)，35 岁，是与汽车相撞的固定卡车的司机，他否认对他阻碍交通自由的指控。 奥贡州汽车交通部门的检查员克里斯托弗·阿贾伊·泰沃告诉法庭，当他到达现场时，受损的雷克萨斯和静止的卡车都已被移走。 但他补充说，警方在路上发现了车祸产生的碎片和卡车上散落在路上的大豆。 阿贾伊说，从雷克萨斯车上找到的唯一物品是一本日志、止痛药和能量饮料，这些物品是在驾驶员一侧发现的。 法庭获悉，事故发生后，警方尚未听取约书亚的声明。 在盘问期间，卡约德的律师就阿贾伊缺乏陈述的问题向阿贾伊提出质疑，阿贾伊回答说“正在努力”，并且他没有联系约书亚，因为他“没有电话号码”。 约书亚出生在沃特福德，他的家族根源在萨加穆——奥贡州的一个小镇，靠近坠机地点。 碰撞发生后，这位拳击手在社交媒体上向加米和阿约德勒致敬。 “我只是和他们一起散步，和他们开玩笑，甚至不知道上帝让我和伟人在一起。

reflection.en: The court heard that the driver of the car carrying boxer Anthony Joshua was attempting to overtake another vehicle when the crash occurred, resulting in the deaths of two friends. This tragic event serves as a somber reminder of the destructive consequences that can arise from actions taken in haste or recklessness, echoing the ancient wisdom that violence...
reflection.zh: 法庭获悉，载有拳击手安东尼·约书亚的汽车司机在试图超车时发生车祸，导致两名朋友丧生。这一悲惨事件令人痛心地提醒我们，仓促或鲁莽的行为可能带来毁灭性的后果，呼应了“以暴力对待他人者，终将遭受暴力”的古老智慧。

verse.textEn: All who draw the sword will die by the sword.
verse.textZh: 凡动刀的，必死在刀下。

title.en: Vance's Antichrist comments are a 'common belief', his friend tells BBC
title.zh: 万斯关于反基督者的言论，其朋友告诉BBC是“普遍的信念”

summary.en: US Vice-President JD Vance recently discussed his religious views on a Christian podcast, speculating about the Antichrist and the end times. His friend, Rod Dreher, told the BBC that such beliefs are common among many Americans and that Vance's comments would not harm his political standing.
summary.zh: 美国副总统JD·万斯最近在一个基督教播客上谈论了他的宗教观点，推测了关于反基督者和末世的言论。他的朋友罗德·德雷尔告诉BBC，这种信仰在许多美国人中很普遍，并且万斯的言论不会损害他的政治地位。

body.en:
Recent remarks by US Vice-President JD Vance about the Antichrist and "the end times" are a "very, very common belief", one of his friends says.

Vance recently mused on his religious views while responding to a question on a Christian podcast. He said he would "not [be] shocked if the Antichrist was walking among us" and speculated on whether the end of the world was nigh.

His friend Rod Dreher, a conservative writer, rejected any suggestion that the comments would harm the vice-president. He told the BBC's Today programme: "Most Americans who are inclined to vote Republican already believe this stuff."

In his podcast comments, Vance also clarified that such thoughts did not preoccupy him.

In Christianity, the "end times" phrase refers to theories about what will happen at the end of the world. Many churches believe God has a divine plan for the end of everything.

Meanwhile, the Antichrist is seen as the enemy of God who appears during the final phase of the world's existence and takes it over.

Vance, who became a Catholic as an adult, reflected on these topics during a recent podcast discussion with Bryce Crawford, a US Christian podcaster.

"Do I think that we're in the end times? I don't know," he said in response to a Crawford question on the subject. "And I think that it's probably bad for me spiritually to focus too much on it, because there are, like, things you gotta do.

"I gotta be good to my wife. I gotta be good to my kids. I have to be as good of a leader as I can for the United States of America."

The vice-president continued by saying: "I think that there are, like, things about the world that make me feel, like, not shocked if the Antichrist was walking among us."

But Vance reiterated that he was preoccupied with being vice-president, explaining: "What I'm trying to focus on is doing as much of God's work as possible right now."

Reacting to Vance's comments about the Antichrist, Dreher said: "This might sound bonkers to someone who is outside the Christian religion, but it is a very, very common belief within Christianity."

He said his friend was simply reflecting that the world appeared to be going "crazy" through the rapid development of AI and ongoing conflicts.

Dreher, who was present when Vance was received into the Catholic Church, said Ronald Reagan had made similar comments when he was the US president, and that this was seen as "perfectly normal" by his voters.

Vance converted to Catholicism in 2019, then in his mid-30s, and has described how the Church resonated with his family and social values and his conservative politics.

Since becoming vice-president, he has occasionally tangled with Pope Leo and his papal predecessor Francis, on issues including the Trump administration's immigration policy.

Vance is due...
body.zh: 美国副总统万斯最近关于反基督者和“末日”的言论是“非常非常普遍的信念”，他的一位朋友说。 万斯最近在基督教播客上回答问题时思考了他的宗教观点。他说，如果敌基督者行走在我们中间，他“不会感到震惊”，并猜测世界末日是否即将来临。 他的朋友罗德·德雷尔（Rod Dreher）是一位保守派作家，他拒绝接受任何有关这些言论会伤害副总统的说法。他告诉英国广播公司的“今日”节目：“大多数倾向于投票给共和党的美国人已经相信了这些东西。” 万斯在播客评论中还澄清说，他并没有想到这些想法。 在基督教中，“末日”一词指的是关于世界末日将发生什么的理论。许多教会相信上帝对一切的终结有一个神圣的计划。 与此同时，敌基督者被视为上帝的敌人，他在世界存在的最后阶段出现并接管了世界。 成年后成为天主教徒的万斯在最近与美国基督教播客布莱斯·克劳福德的播客讨论中反思了这些话题。 “我认为我们已经处于末世了吗？我不知道，”他在回答克劳福德关于这个问题的问题时说道。 “我认为过度关注这件事对我的精神上可能是不好的，因为有些事情是你必须做的。 “我必须对我的妻子好。我必须对我的孩子们好。我必须尽我所能成为美利坚合众国的优秀领导者。” 副总统继续说道：“我认为，如果敌基督者走在我们中间，世界上有一些事情让我感到不感到震惊。” 但万斯重申，他全神贯注于担任副总统，并解释说：“我现在的重点是尽可能多地做上帝的工作。” 德雷尔在回应万斯关于反基督者的评论时说：“对于基督教以外的人来说，这可能听起来很疯狂，但这是基督教内部非常非常普遍的信仰。” 他说，他的朋友只是反映，由于人工智能的快速发展和持续不断的冲突，世界似乎变得“疯狂”。 万斯被天主教堂接纳时在场的德雷尔表示，罗纳德·里根在担任美国总统时也曾发表过类似言论，他的选民认为这“完全正常”。 万斯于 2019 年 30 多岁时皈依天主教，并描述了教会如何与他的家庭、社会价值观以及他的保守政治产生共鸣。 自成为副总统以来，他偶尔会在特朗普政府的移民政策等问题上与教皇利奥及其前任教皇弗朗西斯发生争执。 万斯因...

reflection.en: James 3:5 speaks of how "the tongue is a fire, a world of unrighteousness." The US Vice-President's casual remarks on a podcast, amplified by a friend's interview, quickly became a news item, illustrating how words, even when spoken lightly, can ignite widespread discussion and debate. This reminds us of the power of our speech. Whether in casual...
reflection.zh: 雅各书3:5说：“舌头就是火，是世界的不义。”美国副总统在播客上随意的言论，经过朋友在采访中的放大，迅速成为新闻焦点，这说明了言语即使是轻率说出的，也能点燃广泛的讨论和辩论。 这提醒我们言语的力量。无论是在闲聊还是在公共平台，我们的言语都很有分量，可能产生意想不到的后果，引发超出我们初衷的广泛讨论。

verse.textEn: The tongue is a small part of the body, but it makes great boasts. Consider what a great forest is set on fire by a small spark.
verse.textZh: 舌头在百体里也是最小的，却能说大话。看哪，最小的火能点着最大的树林。

title.en: Can Hichilema heal Zambia's political divide?
title.zh: 希奇莱马能否弥合赞比亚的政治分歧？

summary.en: Zambian President Hakainde Hichilema begins his second term following a disputed election that exposed significant political divisions. His administration faces the dual challenge of unifying the nation while also addressing concerns regarding political freedoms.
summary.zh: 赞比亚总统哈凯恩德·希奇莱马在一次有争议的选举暴露了深刻的政治分歧后，开始了第二个任期。他的政府面临着团结国家并解决对政治自由担忧的双重挑战。

body.en:
The Zambian president starts a second term after a contested election exposed deep political divisions. His challenge now is to unite the country while addressing concerns over political freedoms.

Zambian President Hakainde Hichilema was sworn in for a second five-year term on Tuesday.

For decades, Zambia has worn its peaceful transfers of power almost like a badge of honor in a region where elections have too often ended in disputed results, violence or leaders refusing to leave. Hichilema's own victory in 2021 appeared to strengthen that reputation.

Hichilema begins his second term after a disputed election , with his main challenger facing treason charges , opposition supporters questioning the credibility of the vote and controversy surrounding the closure of courts during the crucial window for election petitions.

Hichilema has promised reconciliation. But for a president who once sat on the other side of power as an opposition leader and treason suspect himself, the test now is whether those words will be matched by the political space he gives his opponents.

Ngobola Cengelo Muyembe, a political, business and social analyst, told DW that reconciliation must begin by recognizing that a significant part of the electorate backed someone else.

"You have to remember that in every 10 people that voted, four people voted for the other side," Muyembe said, noting that during the president's inaugural address, he spoke about reconciliation and uniting people. "But that message can only resonate if what is on the ground reflects what is being spoken about."

Raymond, a self-employed Zambian who asked that his full name not be used, told DW that Hichilema should look beyond who supported him at the ballot box and govern across Zambia's political and ethnic divisions.

"The president, congratulations! Don't think about people who voted for you, didn't vote for you. One Zambia, one nation, one city," Raymond said. "Real change in mines and agriculture. The mines want us Zambians to be benefiting. Even your Tonga, your Bemba, you are all Zambians."

Artist Mazuba Nzabuka told DW he also wants Hichilema to govern those who supported him and those who did not, while giving young people a greater voice.

"Going forward, he is going to do the promises left behind. He is a president for all people," said Nzabuka. "Those who did not vote for him, those who voted for him. We are the same people. The five years going forward, our voices can be heard. Look after the youths."

But reconciliation will have to contend with the political fallout from the election.

Zambia returned to multiparty democracy in 1991 and has since witnessed several changes of governing parties through elections. Hichilema himself benefited from that tradition when he defeated incumbent...
body.zh: 赞比亚总统在一场有争议的选举暴露出深刻的政治分歧后开始了第二个任期。他现在的挑战是团结国家，同时解决对政治自由的担忧。 赞比亚总统哈坎德·希奇莱马周二宣誓就职，开始第二个五年任期。 几十年来，赞比亚的和平权力移交几乎就像是一个荣誉徽章，该地区的选举经常以有争议的结果、暴力或领导人拒绝离开而告终。希奇莱马自己在 2021 年的胜利似乎强化了这一声誉。 希奇莱马在一场有争议的选举后开始了他的第二个任期，他的主要挑战者面临叛国罪指控，反对派支持者质疑投票的可信度，以及围绕选举请愿的关键窗口期间关闭法院的争议。 希奇莱马承诺和解。但对于一位曾经作为反对派领袖站​​在权力另一边并怀疑自己叛国的总统来说，现在的考验是这些话是否会与他给予对手的政治空间相匹配。 政治、商业和社会分析师恩戈博拉·森杰洛·穆延贝 (Ngobola Cengelo Muyembe) 告诉德国之声，和解必须首先认识到很大一部分选民支持其他人。 穆延贝说：“你必须记住，每 10 个人投票，就有 4 个人投票给对方。”他指出，在总统的就职演说中，他谈到了和解和团结人民。 “但只有当实际情况反映了所谈论的内容时，这一信息才能产生共鸣。” 赞比亚个体经营者雷蒙德要求不透露自己的全名，他告诉德国之声，希奇莱马应该超越投票箱中支持他的人，并跨越赞比亚的政治和种族分歧进行治理。 “总统，恭喜你！不要去想那些投票给你的人，那些没有投票给你的人。一个赞比亚，一个国家，一座城市，”雷蒙德说。 “矿山和农业发生了真正的变化。矿山希望我们赞比亚人受益。甚至你们的汤加、你们的本巴，你们都是赞比亚人。” 艺术家马祖巴·恩扎布卡 (Mazuba Nzabuka) 告诉德国之声，他还希望希奇莱马能够统治那些支持他和不支持他的人，同时让年轻人有更大的发言权。 恩扎布卡说：“展望未来，他将履行留下的承诺。他是所有人的总统。” “那些没有投票给他的人，那些投票给他的人。我们是同一个人。未来五年，我们的声音可以被听到。照顾年轻人。” 但和解必须应对选举带来的政治影响。 赞比亚于1991年恢复多党民主，此后通过选举多次更换执政党。当希奇莱马击败现任总统时，他本人也从这一传统中受益。

reflection.en: In Zambia, President Hichilema faces the daunting task of bridging deep political divides after a contentious election. The pursuit of unity and the safeguarding of political freedoms are critical for his second term, echoing the ancient wisdom that righteous rulers bring stability and hope, while the absence of justice leads to ruin.
reflection.zh: 在赞比亚，希奇莱马总统面临着在一次有争议的选举后弥合深刻政治分歧的艰巨任务。追求团结和保障政治自由对他第二个任期至关重要，这呼应了古老的智慧：公义的统治者带来稳定和希望，而缺乏公义则导致毁灭。

verse.textEn: When the righteous thrive, the people rejoice; when the wicked rule, the people groan.
verse.textZh: 义人增多，民就喜乐；恶人掌权，民就叹息。

title.en: Clean-up begins as authorities in Nepal assess how many homes have been lost
title.zh: 尼泊尔清理工作开始，当局评估房屋损失情况

summary.en: Authorities report that thousands of homes have been destroyed, washed away, or buried under debris and mud in Nepal. Rescuers are searching for workers trapped in tunnels following a glacier collapse that caused a massive deluge.
summary.zh: 当局报告称，尼泊尔已有数千所房屋被毁、被冲走或被瓦砾和泥浆掩埋。在冰川崩塌引发大规模洪水后，救援人员正在搜寻被困在隧道中的工人。

body.en:
Nepal will have to rebuild around 20,000 houses in flood-ravaged areas, authorities said on Thursday, as rescuers continued to search for workers trapped in tunnels linked to hydropower projects and thousands remain missing after last week’s catastrophe.

A glacier collapse on 26 August sent a deluge of ice, rock and mud sweeping through the impoverished nation's border region with China, wiping out settlements and villages and leaving few houses standing and undamaged.

"Our preliminary estimates are that 7,500 houses have been completely destroyed, either washed away or buried under debris and mud," Dharma Raj Upreti, chief of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, told Reuters.

Even houses still standing were not habitable, Upreti said, with authorities estimating that around 20,000 houses would have to be rebuilt in different, safer locations.

At least 1,252 people were killed in Nepal last week as houses, streets and schools in towns and villages near the border with China's Tibet were swept away. More than 4,200 people are still missing and thousands more displaced.

More than 9,300 Nepali army troops are on the ground in the affected areas of Timure in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Chitwan and Nawalparasi East, coordinating search and rescue of the injured and helping with management of bodies, clearing blocked roads, and providing emergency medical treatment, an army statement said on Thursday.

An Australian medical student whose partner went missing near the Nepal-China border urged tech companies to do more to help find him and others caught up in the disaster by sharing tracking data that could narrow the search areas for rescue teams.

At least 583 foreign nationals were missing in the floods, Nepal said on Thursday, many of them pilgrims and trekkers.

An army officer who spoke on condition of anonymity as he is not authorised to speak to the media, said the search was continuing with experts from India, South Korea and China for at least 900 survivors believed to be trapped in the tunnels related to hydropower projects.

"The search-and-rescue operation will continue as long as there is any hope of finding survivors. Even if there are no survivors, we will recover the dead bodies," he said.

Army spokesperson Raja Ram Basnet said two bodies had been recovered from the tunnel of Langtang Khola hydropower plant.

Australia pledged additional support and said it would also share telecommunications data with Nepali authorities.

body.zh: 尼泊尔当局周四表示，尼泊尔将不得不在遭受洪水破坏的地区重建约 20,000 所房屋，救援人员仍在继续搜寻被困在与水电项目相关的隧道中的工人，上周的灾难后仍有数千人失踪。 8 月 26 日，冰川崩塌，大量冰、岩石和泥浆席卷了这个贫穷国家与中国的边境地区，摧毁了定居点和村庄，几乎没有房屋完好无损。 国家减少灾害风险和管理局局长达玛·拉杰·乌普雷蒂 (Dharma Raj Upreti) 告诉路透社：“我们初步估计，有 7,500 所房屋已被完全摧毁，要么被冲走，要么被埋在废墟和泥土中。” 乌普雷蒂说，即使仍然矗立的房屋也不适合居住，当局估计大约 20,000 栋房屋必须在不同的、更安全的地点重建。 上周，尼泊尔与中国西藏接壤的边境城镇和村庄的房屋、街道和学校被冲毁，造成至少 1,252 人死亡。仍有 4,200 多人失踪，数千人流离失所。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 周四军方声明称，超过 9,300 名尼泊尔陆军士兵在拉苏瓦、努瓦科特、达丁、奇特万和纳瓦尔帕拉西东部的蒂穆雷受影响地区进行地面救援，协调伤员搜救工作，帮助处理尸体、清理堵塞的道路并提供紧急医疗救治。 一名澳大利亚医科学生的伴侣在中尼边境附近失踪，他敦促科技公司采取更多措施，通过共享跟踪数据来帮助寻找他和其他陷入灾难的人，从而缩小救援队的搜索范围。 尼泊尔周四表示，至少有 583 名外国人在洪水中失踪，其中许多是朝圣者和徒步旅行者。 一名不愿透露姓名的军官表示，来自印度、韩国和中国的专家正在继续搜寻被困在与水电项目相关的隧道中的至少 900 名幸存者。 “只要有希望找到幸存者，搜救行动就会继续下去。即使没有幸存者，我们也会打捞尸体，”他说。 陆军发言人 Raja Ram Basnet 表示，已从 Langtang Khola 水电站隧道中找到两具尸体。 澳大利亚承诺提供额外支持，并表示还将与尼泊尔当局共享电信数据。 外媒称，中国已向尼泊尔提供第三批援助物资，包括帐篷、毛毯、医用防护服、卫星通讯设备等。

reflection.en: The news from Nepal paints a stark picture of devastation, with thousands of homes lost and many people missing after a catastrophic glacier collapse. In the face of such overwhelming loss, the ancient words of Lamentations offer a profound perspective: "The steadfast love of Yahweh never ceases; his mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning;...
reflection.zh: 尼泊尔传来的消息描绘了一幅触目惊心的毁灭景象，一场灾难性的冰川崩塌导致数千房屋被毁，许多人失踪。面对如此巨大的损失，古老的《耶利米哀歌》提供了深刻的视角：“雅伟的慈爱永不枯竭；他的怜悯每早更新；你的诚实极其广大。”...

verse.textEn: Because of Yahweh's great love we are not consumed, for his compassions never fail. They are new every morning.
verse.textZh: 我们不至消灭，是出于雅伟诸般的慈爱；是因他的怜悯不至断绝。每早晨这都是新的。

title.en: After Trump's Greenland threats, Denmark is boosting its Arctic presence with conscripts
title.zh: 在特朗普威胁格陵兰后，丹麦正通过征兵加强其北极存在

summary.en: Denmark has pledged to strengthen Arctic defenses after acknowledging years of underinvestment in the semi-autonomous territory.
summary.zh: 丹麦在承认多年来对半自治领土的投资不足后，承诺加强北极防御。

body.en:
For the first time in recent history, Danish conscripts have been deployed to Greenland, as Denmark moves to bolster its presence in the Arctic after US demands to acquire the territory.

US President Donald Trump has repeatedly sought to acquire the semi-autonomous Danish island, citing national security concerns and accusing Denmark of neglecting Arctic defence. Denmark and Greenland have firmly rejected the idea.

The conscripts are part of the first cohort under Denmark's new extended conscription program, aimed at producing soldiers capable of operating in one of the kingdom's most strategically important and challenging regions.

"It shows presence that we're here and not just thinking of our own skin. And also thinking of the people in Greenland," 19-year-old conscript David told the Reuters news agency.

Denmark has pledged billions of dollars to strengthen Arctic defences after Denmark's defence minister acknowledged years of underinvestment in the region.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"Of course, we are a part of a bigger picture of the strategic communication about Greenland, but our role here is just to continue the training of the conscripts, the soldiers, and get more experience with the training in the Arctic terrain and climate," company commander captain Laura Jepsen said.

The conscripts are taking part in Arctic Endurance, a Danish military exercise that trains soldiers for combat and survival in extreme cold-weather conditions.

The drill forms part of Arctic Sentry, a NATO mission launched this year to strengthen the alliance's Arctic presence and ease tensions within NATO after Trump's remarks about Greenland.

Russia, which maintains the Arctic's largest military footprint, has criticised NATO's growing activity in the region, describing it as a direct security threat that increases the risk of confrontation.

China has increased its activity in the mineral-rich region, mostly in partnership with Russia.

Training north of the Arctic Circle, the conscripts moved through a landscape of bare rock and open expanses with no trees in sight.

"I think it sends a message that Denmark is reinforcing itself for the future," Anton, 22, one of the conscripts, said.

body.zh: 在美国要求获得格陵兰岛后，丹麦采取行动加强其在北极的存在，这是近代历史上首次将丹麦应征入伍者部署到格陵兰岛。 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普多次以国家安全为由寻求收购这个半自治的丹麦岛屿，并指责丹麦忽视北极防御。丹麦和格陵兰岛坚决拒绝了这一想法。 这些应征入伍者是丹麦新的延长征兵计划的第一批士兵的一部分，该计划旨在培养能够在该国战略上最重要和最具挑战性的地区之一作战的士兵。 19 岁的新兵大卫告诉路透社，“这表明我们在这里，不仅仅考虑自己的皮肤。还考虑格陵兰岛的人民。” 在丹麦国防部长承认多年来对该地区的投资不足后，丹麦承诺提供数十亿美元来加强北极防御。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 “当然，我们是格陵兰战略沟通大局的一部分，但我们在这里的作用只是继续对应征入伍的士兵进行训练，并在北极地形和气候下的训练中获得更多经验，”连长劳拉·杰普森上尉说。 应征入伍的士兵正在参加丹麦的“北极耐力”军事演习，训练士兵在极端寒冷的天气条件下作战和生存。 这次演习是北约今年启动的“北极哨兵”任务的一部分，旨在加强该联盟在北极的存在，并在特朗普发表有关格陵兰岛的言论后缓解北约内部的紧张局势。 俄罗斯在北极地区拥有最大的军事足迹，它批评北约在该地区日益增长的活动，称其为直接的安全威胁，增加了对抗的风险。 中国增加了在矿产丰富地区的活动，主要是与俄罗斯合作。 在北极圈以北的训练中，应征入伍者穿过一片光秃秃的岩石和一片空旷的地方，看不到任何树木。 “我认为这传达了一个信息，即丹麦正在为未来加强自身实力，”22 岁的应征入伍者之一安东说。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

reflection.en: In response to perceived threats and past neglect, Denmark is increasing its military presence in Greenland. This news prompts reflection on the global tendency to rely on armaments. Isaiah's vision offers a counter-narrative, imagining a future where military might is transformed into tools for peace and productivity, a stark contrast to the current...
reflection.zh: 为应对感知到的威胁和过去的忽视，丹麦正在增加其在格陵兰的军事存在。这一消息促使人们反思全球依赖军备的趋势。以赛亚的异象提供了一个反叙事，描绘了一个军事力量被转化为和平与生产力工具的未来，这与当前地缘政治对防御的关注形成了鲜明对比。

verse.textEn: They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks.
verse.textZh: 他们要将刀打成犁头，把枪打成镰刀。

title.en: Why the Lindsay Clancy filicide trial has captured global attention
title.zh: 为何林赛·克兰西的弑子案引发全球关注

summary.en: The 36-year-old has pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity in the strangling deaths of her three children.
summary.zh: 这位36岁的女子在被控扼死她的三个孩子一案中，以精神失常为由提出无罪辩护。

body.en:
The case of Lindsay Clancy in the United States has captured international attention due to its horrific and complex nature, with one expert telling SBS News that the intrigue reflects a "call to change society".

The 36-year-old mother of three claimed to be suffering from postpartum psychosis when she strangled her three young children to death in their home in Duxbury, Massachusetts, in January 2023.

She then cut her wrists and jumped from a second-story window, leaving her paralysed from the waist down and using a wheelchair.

Clancy has pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity, saying she heard a voice ordering her to kill her children.

Prosecutors have rejected her argument, saying she had planned to murder her children and was able to understand the consequences of her actions.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The five-week trial has come down to five days and nearly 30 hours of deliberation, with the case currently deadlocked as jurors say they cannot reach a unanimous decision.

The labour and delivery nurse faces a mandatory life sentence if found guilty, and could be committed to a psychiatric facility indefinitely if acquitted on mental health grounds.

Internet sleuths, TikTok detectives, and social media discussions have pored over every aspect of the case, with both defenders and critics staking out their own various theories about exactly what happened.

Such ongoing digital scrutiny is reminiscent of other murder trials involving female perpetrators and, in some cases, family members.

In the same year Clancy strangled her children, Australian Erin Patterson laced beef Wellington with lethal death cap mushrooms and served it to her estranged husband's parents, his aunt, and his aunt's husband.

In 2020, nurse Lucy Letby was convicted of murdering seven babies in the 2010s at the neonatal unit where she worked in Britain .

Decades prior, Lindy Chamberlain was convicted of murdering her own child and spent years behind bars before a royal commission and a final coroner's validated that a dingo had taken her baby, as she had always said.

Rachel Franks, honorary associate lecturer at the University of Newcastle and expert in true crime and crime fiction, told SBS News that such cases draw public attention because they upend our perception of violent perpetrators.

"The public is often much more drawn to cases where children are victims because the injustice of it is just so obvious.

"It is particularly disturbing for us when the perpetrators are women, because we are so trained to accept women as protectors, as the nurturers."

The legal system grapples with questions of responsibility and sanity, while society is left to confront the devastating consequences of such a tragedy. This...

title.en: The world is expected to overshoot a critical climate target. But there's still hope
title.zh: 全球预计将突破关键气候目标，但仍存希望

summary.en: A new United Nations report indicates the world will likely surpass 1.5C of warming by 2030. Despite this concerning projection, experts suggest that immediate actions and political will can still mitigate the worst effects and shape a climate-safe future.
summary.zh: 一份新的联合国报告指出，世界可能在2030年前超过1.5摄氏度的升温目标。尽管这一预测令人担忧，但专家们认为，当前的行动和政治意愿仍能减轻最严重的影响，并塑造一个气候安全的未来。

body.en:
That's no longer possible, according to a new United Nations report. We will likely pass 1.5C in 2030. That's not good news for anyone, least of all Australia's Pacific Island neighbours who face rapidly rising seas.

In response to the report, Palau's President Surangel Whipps Jr said: "It is hard to overstate the depth of emotion for those of us living on the front-line after having fought so hard to put the 1.5 degree limit at the heart of the Paris Agreement … calls for greater ambition are no longer enough — we need to see an urgent and unprecedented increase in political will and investment in a climate safe future."

The small silver lining is that it's still possible for this to be a temporary overshoot of the target.

If nations redouble their efforts to phase out fossil fuels and reduce other sources of emissions, they could limit peak warming to 1.8C and then use carbon removal methods to bring temperatures back to 1.5C or below this century.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

In 2026, the world is already about 1.4C warmer than pre-industrial levels, and the damage and death toll from climate-boosted disasters is ramping up.

The United Kingdom is warning of possible food shortages amid a historic drought.

Wildfires hit new areas in France and Spain, while glaciers are melting rapidly and the oceans are at their hottest level on record.

The enormous El Niño event emerging in the Pacific is likely to bring major disruption. Every fraction of a degree makes things worse.

There are no good outcomes if we remain above 1.5C. Urgent cuts to emissions and efforts to protect the most vulnerable are our best remaining options. Failure to do so risks irreversible harm.

The 2015 Paris Agreement established a shared goal for the world: keep the rise in global average temperatures above pre-industrial levels "well below" 2C and "pursue efforts" to hold warming to 1.5C.

This goal was set based on expert scientific assessments that warming of more than 2C would be dangerous and that limiting warming to 1.5C was necessary to minimise climate risks.

Pacific nations fought hard to include 1.5C in the agreement, arguing it was essential for their communities to "stay alive" in the face of rising sea levels and other climate-fuelled threats.

Last year, the world's top court — the International Court of Justice — ruled that 1.5C is the primary temperature limit nations have committed to work towards.

This ruling means that if governments fail to act as ambitiously as they can, they could be sued in international courts.

In May this year, a majority of nations voted in the UN General Assembly to endorse the court's...
body.zh: 根据联合国的一份新报告，这已不再可能。到 2030 年，气温可能会超过 1.5 摄氏度。这对任何人来说都不是好消息，尤其是面临海平面迅速上升的澳大利亚太平洋岛屿邻国。 帕劳总统小苏兰吉尔·惠普斯在回应这份报告时表示：“我们这些生活在第一线的人们，在为将 1.5 度气温限制纳入《巴黎协定》的核心而进行了艰苦奋斗后，其情感之深怎么形容都不为过……仅仅呼吁更大的雄心已经不够了——我们需要看到政治意愿和投资以前所未有的方式紧迫增加，以实现气候安全的未来。” 一线希望是，这仍然有可能暂时超出目标。 如果各国加倍努力逐步淘汰化石燃料并减少其他排放源，他们可以将峰值升温限制在 1.8 摄氏度，然后使用碳去除方法将本世纪气温恢复到 1.5 摄氏度或以下。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 到 2026 年，世界气温已比工业化前水平高出约 1.4 摄氏度，气候引发的灾难造成的损失和死亡人数正在不断增加。 英国警告称，在历史性干旱期间可能出现粮食短缺。 野火袭击了法国和西班牙的新地区，冰川正在迅速融化，海洋达到有记录以来的最热水平。 太平洋地区出现的巨大厄尔尼诺事件可能会带来重大破坏。每一度的一小部分都会让事情变得更糟。 如果温度保持在 1.5 摄氏度以上，不会有什么好结果。紧急削减排放和努力保护最弱势群体是我们剩下的最佳选择。如果不这样做，可能会造成不可逆转的伤害。 2015年《巴黎协定》为世界确立了一个共同目标：将全球平均气温上升幅度控制在工业化前水平“远低于”2摄氏度，并“努力”将升温控制在1.5摄氏度以内。 这一目标是根据专家科学评估制定的，专家的科学评估认为升温超过 2 摄氏度将是危险的，并且有必要将升温限制在 1.5 摄氏度，以尽量减少气候风险。 太平洋国家为将 1.5℃ 纳入协议进行了艰苦的斗争，认为面对海平面上升和其他气候引发的威胁，它们的社区必须“生存”。 去年，世界最高法院——国际法院——裁定 1.5 摄氏度是各国承诺努力实现的主要温度限制。 这项裁决意味着，如果政府未能尽其所能采取雄心勃勃的行动，他们可能会在国际法庭上被起诉。 今年五月，大多数国家在联合国大会上投票支持了法院的...

This echoes Jeremiah 29:11, a promise of hope and a future even when circumstances...
